learning_path.title: Pivot-Style Summaries (Grouping + Aggregation) — From Question to Table
learning_path.abstract: Learn the workflow for pivot-style summaries: define the business question (what to group by, what to aggregate, and what the output should look like), then prepare the source table (clean headers, one category column, one measure column). You’ll practice designing a summary table that computes totals/averages/counts by category, and you’ll debug common issues like inconsistent category values or choosing the wrong aggregation. Includes a quick cheat-sheet for “group by” vs “aggregate” and a mini checklist for validating results.

desired_outcome_when_completed.name: Pivot-style summaries using grouping and aggregations

learning_path.title: Reference-Accurate Formulas for Summary Tables (Relative vs Absolute)
learning_path.abstract: Build and verify formulas inside summary outputs: compute derived metrics (e.g., percent of total, rate per unit) using correct relative vs absolute references. You’ll practice with 2–3 scenarios: (1) totals by category, (2) aggregations feeding a “share of total” column, and (3) rates that require locking denominators. The session emphasizes procedural accuracy: show the formula, explain each reference, then run a mini task where you predict what changes when you copy/fill down.

desired_outcome_when_completed.name: Correct relative vs absolute formulas in summary contexts
Creating derived metrics from aggregated data

learning_path.title: Sorting & Filtering for Focused Analysis (Before You Summarize)
learning_path.abstract: Use sorting and filtering to answer targeted questions before building summaries. You’ll learn to (a) filter to the relevant slice (date ranges, statuses, departments), (b) sort to reveal ranking patterns (top/bottom, highest averages), and (c) ensure the summarized output matches the filtered subset. Includes interactive exercises that require quick sanity checks (row counts, totals consistency) and a short “common mistakes” list (filter not applied, mixed data types, sort breaking alignment).

desired_outcome_when_completed.name: Sorting and filtering data to answer questions
Validating that summaries reflect the intended filtered subset

learning_path.title: Charts from Aggregated/Filtered Data (Bar/Line/Pie/Scatter Rules)
learning_path.abstract: Select and generate effective basic charts from your pivot-style summaries. You’ll practice choosing the right chart type based on the data intent: bar for comparisons across categories, line for trends over time, pie for composition (with caveats), scatter for relationships (with axes meaning). You’ll also learn how to correctly set ranges/series so the chart reflects the filtered/aggregated table. Includes a quick chart-selection cheat-sheet and a mini task to produce one chart with correct labels and readable scales.
associated_skills: Effective basic charts selection and creation

desired_outcome_when_completed.name: Selecting and generating effective basic charts from aggregated data
Producing readable charts with correct series/ranges

learning_path.title: Presentation Best Practices: Make the Sheet Tell the Story
learning_path.abstract: Turn your analysis into a presentation-ready spreadsheet. You’ll apply consistent formatting and layout: clear titles, descriptive axis labels, legend where needed, number formats (thousands separators, decimals), and spacing between input → calculation → output. Includes interactive checklist-based refinement: start with an “okay” sheet and improve it to be understandable to a non-author in 60 seconds. You’ll finish by producing a final packaged view: summary table + one or two charts + a short interpretation sentence.

desired_outcome_when_completed.name: Communicating analysis with coherent table + chart narrative
